The '''Solaran Alphabet''', also known as '''Sunline''', is the standard modern writing system for the [[Solaran Language]]. It was created in the 1890s as part of Solara's national literacy reforms and became one of the main tools of modern Solaran administration, education, publishing, and commerce.

== Background ==

Before Sunline, elite religious and legal writing relied on the older [[Solra]] abugida. That script carried ceremonial prestige but was difficult to teach at mass scale. As Solara industrialized in the late nineteenth century, parliament, schools, publishers, and state offices needed a simpler writing system for a wider literate population.

The [[Solaran Parliament]] commissioned the new alphabet in 1895 through the [[Education Reform Act of 1895]]. The reform was presented as an educational project, but it also had political importance: a common written standard supported national integration across a large parliamentary state.

== Adoption ==

Sunline was tested in schools for three years and officially adopted in 1898. Parliament's education committee handled the testing period in the current draft structure, and the [[Solaran Language Office]] is source-attested with the 1898 official standard.

After adoption, the [[Solaran Ministry of Education]] is source-attested with 1899 implementation guidance, and the [[Solaran Academy of Linguistics]] with post-adoption study in 1900.

The reform did not abolish the Elder Tongue. Instead, it created a practical public alphabet for Solaran while leaving [[Solra]] in ceremonial, temple, legal, and specialist use.

== Structure ==

The source describes Sunline as a 26-letter, left-to-right alphabet derived from simplified and rotated strokes of the classical script. Vowels and consonants are written as full letters on the same line, with spacing and punctuation used in the modern printed style.

The extracted letter tables contain corrupted characters and duplicate categories. This draft preserves the broad 26-letter claim but does not treat the imported table as publication-ready canon.

== Public Use ==

By the twentieth century, Sunline was used in primary and secondary education, government documents, newspapers, business records, public signs, legal notices, and ordinary correspondence.

The alphabet helped make Solaran national identity visible in everyday life. It also allowed state institutions to speak to the public directly while older Solra remained available for ritual formulae, archives, and formal state symbolism.

== Canon Notes ==

The 1895-1898 reform is useful pre-1994 canon because it explains why Solara could combine ceremonial tradition with mass literacy before the [[Avant Great War]] and the [[Solara-Khalindar War]].

Full phonetic values, glyph names, and letter forms need an orthography review before publication because the extracted dump includes mojibake and inconsistent tables.
